status_summary: VA reports faster disability claims processing, and VA officials quoted in trade press credit automation for at least part of the gain; Executive Order 14426 (signed 2026-09-08) directs VA and the Department of War to share records, build AI-enabled benefits tools and review IT contracts. VA says average processing time fell from 141.5 days on 2025-01-20 to 75.6 days in September 2026, the backlog fell by more than 70 percent and accuracy is about 94 percent (VA's figures; the House committee's ranking member has attributed the gains partly to the system working through the post-PACT Act surge, per MeriTalk). Nextgov reported on 2025-08-13 that VA runs an Express 30 Claims Pilot using automated decision support for claim types that can be decided within 30 days, which resembles the Mandate's first-claim pilot but was not described as a general 30-day commitment for first claims. The Mandate's other tools were not confirmed: no formal public quarterly targets, no expansion of contract medical exams (contractors already perform most exams, VA has said it wants fewer unnecessary exams, and the main contracts are reported due for rebid after 2026-12-31), and no improper-payment measures.

timeline.event: Nextgov reports a record 2.52 million claims processed in FY2025 to date and a backlog down 37 percent since 2025-01-20; a VA spokesperson credits automated decision support and review summaries, and the report describes the Express 30 Claims Pilot.

Nextgov reports that VA's press secretary says machine learning pre-populates parts of Toxic Exposure Risk Activity memos, the Automated Decision Support tool will cover more condition and claim types, the tool does not make claim decisions, and the backlog fell 61 percent over the past year (VA's figures as reported); the article does not mention an Express 30 pilot, contract exams or performance targets.

Trade press (The Capitol Forum) reports that four contractors hold the disability exam contracts that began 2025-01-01, that they expire 2026-12-31 and are expected to be rebid, that about 90 percent of exams are done by contractors, and that VA's Secretary said in December 2025 VA wants to curb unnecessary exams.
timeline.source: The Capitol Forum (copy hosted by veteransdisabilityinfo.com)

timeline.event: At a House Veterans' Affairs Committee hearing on the claims backlog, VA's principal deputy under secretary for benefits says automation handles routine tasks such as gathering records and routing claims and that humans make every decision; VA reports 80.7 days average processing time and a backlog under 100,000 (VA figures). Hearing date per a VFW statement; article dated 2026-04-16.

President signs Executive Order 14426, Accelerating Access to Veterans' Benefits and Employment Opportunities (published 2026-09-11, 91 FR 58003): within 30 days the Department of War shares personnel and treatment records with VA at discharge; within 120 days VA and War review and modify relevant IT contracts and require interoperability; within 180 days they stand up updated IT systems and AI-enabled benefits tools; implementation is subject to appropriations.

VA announces more than 3 million disability claims processed in FY2026, average decision time of 75.6 days, a backlog down more than 70 percent since 2025-01-20 and accuracy of 94 percent (VA figures, figures as of 2026-09-18).

VA's Veterans Benefits Administration claims data page links a weekly workload report dated 2026-09-28 and shows 670,845 pending rating-bundle disability compensation and pension claims, of which 74,448 are in the backlog (pending more than 125 days); the page gives no average processing time and no baseline (VA figures).

VA announces a pilot to speed access to services, care and benefits; it concerns faster VA.gov account setup at six facilities rather than a 30-day first-claim commitment (title-level information from the VA press room).

title: Speed disability claims: performance targets, Express 30 pilot, contract exams, automation
uncertainties: Processing-time, backlog and accuracy figures are VA's own and were not independently checked (VA's figures differ slightly by date: 80.7 days in April 2026, 76.1 days in the 2026-09-08 release and 75.6 days in the 2026-09-22 release; a June 2026 local report quoted the Secretary at 77 days). The Express 30 Claims Pilot is described only in a Nextgov report quoting a VA spokesperson; no VA primary page was found (two pass-5 searches, one limited to va.gov and related government domains, returned only a 2017 Decision Ready Claims release that does not use the name, and a March 2026 Nextgov article that does not mention it), so its start date, scope and whether it predates 2025-01-20 are unverified. No source on public quarterly targets or improper-payment results was found. The Capitol Forum item is a paywalled trade report seen through a copy on an advocacy-affiliated site. The 2026-10-07 VA pilot was read at title level only. Searches run: VBA claims, automation and contract exams 2026; VBA contract C&P exam contractors and improper payments; Express 30 pilot. Pass 5: VA's claims data page (weekly report dated 2026-09-28) was read as a VA primary source for inventory and backlog counts but gives no average processing time; contract exam arrangements could not be checked against a primary document (SAM.gov notices were not readable by the research tool), so the contract-exam claims still rest on one trade report.
